extra.message: Session Cookie Set Without Secure Flag — An attacker with network access can intercept the session cookie and impersonate the victim, gaining access to all authenticated resources. [verified: The session cookie is set with secure=False in _set_session_cookie (line 54), allowing transmission over unencrypted HTTP. No HTTPS enforcement or redirect is evident in the code or threat model, enabling session hijacking via network interception.]

Missing CSRF Protection on State-Changing Endpoints — An attacker can force a logged-in victim to perform unintended actions (e.g., upload fraudulent documents, update application status) by tricking them into visiting a malicious web page. [verified: The upload_document endpoint at line 75 does not validate any CSRF token; it only depends on session authentication via get_current_user, leaving it susceptible to cross-site requests with the victim's credentials.]
